# Changelog

Every **resolved issue** of Exudyn, newest first, with the version it produced. The micro version *is* the count of closed issues, so each line below is one version number: 1.10.160 is the 160th issue closed in release 1.10. An issue that was closed without being resolved is in no list: it changed nothing - which is why a release can span more version numbers than it has lines here.

Every entry carries the **type** of the issue, then its **priority** and its **effort** as badges (`LOW EFF` is within 2 hours, `MEDIUM EFF` is within 16 hours, `HIGH EFF` is within 40 hours, `HUGE EFF` is above 40 hours), then who raised it and who resolved it - both omitted when that was Johannes Gerstmayr (JG).

This file is generated; it is written by the tracker whenever an issue closes.

**Only the current release is below.** The issues resolved before it, in the same form, are in the {ref}`issue tracker <sec-issuetracker>` of the documentation, which also lists the open issues and the known bugs; the table that follows is the whole history at a glance.

- **1.13.129** `IMPROVEMENT` `LOW EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` ObjectUserBody: reuse the results of its position and rotation user functions for the same time, coordinates and local position (#3028)
  - description: Measured 2026-10-18 with userRigidBodyTest.py (500 implicit steps, Python user functions counted): per evaluation of the right-hand side, ObjectUserBody calls positionJacobianUserFunction 5 times, positionUserFunction, rotationMatrixUserFunction and rotationJacobianUserFunction 2 times each - the markers, the loads and the connector on it ask for the same values; with the last two results of each function kept, by time, coordinates and local position, 45 % of the calls remain. The derivative of J^T f, which was suspected, costs 2 % (totalJacobian). The results are cleared when a parameter of the body changes.
  - **notes:** ObjectUserBody reuses the results of its position, position Jacobian, rotation matrix and rotation Jacobian user functions for the same time, coordinates and local position, which the markers, loads and connectors on it ask for several times per evaluation; a rigid user body solves 1.4 times (Python) and 1.6 times (symbolic) faster. A change of a parameter or a new Assemble clears the stored results.
  - date resolved: **2026-10-18 10:05**, date raised: 2026-10-18

- **1.13.126** `EXTENSION` `MEDIUM EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` Sparse matrix results of symbolic user functions with the pattern fixed when they are recorded (#3022)
  - description: Mass matrices and Jacobians of ObjectGenericODE2 and ObjectUserBody can be very sparse. A symbolic result esym.SparseMatrix - triplets (row, column, expression) - or an esym.Matrix built from components, whose components that are the constant 0 are known when it is recorded, evaluates into the triplets of the item's MatrixContainer in sparse mode; CopyOrAddTriplets adds them to the system matrix as for a Python function that returns triplets or a scipy matrix. Revision2026c step RG12.3.7.4.
  - **notes:** A matrix result of a symbolic user function built from components is sparse: its components that are the constant 0 are left out when the function is recorded, and the others are added to the system matrix as triplets; a chain of 300 masses with a diagonal mass matrix and a tridiagonal Jacobian solves in 0.26 s against 3.6 s with Python functions building the dense lists.
  - date resolved: **2026-10-17 17:54**, date raised: 2026-10-17
- **1.13.125** `IMPROVEMENT` `MEDIUM EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` Evaluate symbolic matrix expressions into node buffers (#3021)
  - description: Every node of a symbolic matrix expression returns a new matrix; the vector nodes evaluate into their own buffers since \#3006. The same for matrices (EvaluateRef with a mutable buffer per node), so that a symbolic matrix result costs no allocation per call. Revision2026c step RG12.3.7.3.
  - **notes:** Symbolic matrix expressions evaluate into the memory of their nodes: a symbolic user function with a matrix result allocates no memory per call.
  - date resolved: **2026-10-17 17:54**, date raised: 2026-10-17

  - description: revision2026c step RG12.3: a design of the symbolic user functions with vectors and matrices as first-class arguments and the dense linear algebra fully in symbolic, for decision.
  - **notes:** User functions take vectors and matrices as first-class arguments: read-only numpy views for Python user functions, named vectors and matrices for symbolic ones, which compute with numpy's operators and functions; results of any size are returned without allocation, matrix results dense or sparse.
  - date resolved: **2026-10-17 17:54**, date raised: 2026-10-12

  - description: consider functionality to link to dense numpy matrix; possibly by using the allocatedSize in ResizableMatrix to indicate linking rather than allocation

- **1.13.121** `EXTENSION` `LOW EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` Mark an open issue as deferred until a date, so that triage and the plan treat it as waiting on purpose (#3024)

- **1.13.115** `CHANGE` `MEDIUM EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` Make the operators of exudyn.symbolic agree with numpy: \* of two vectors or with a matrix refused, multiply, numpy ufuncs (#3015)
  - description: The operator \* of two symbolic vectors is their scalar product, of matrices and of a matrix and a vector the matrix product; numpy multiplies the components. \* of vectors and matrices raises a TypeError that names dot(), @ and multiply(); exudyn.special.deprecations.symbolicStarProduct restores the old meaning for the transition. Vector.multiply is the product of the components. Numpy's ufuncs (np.multiply, np.sin, np.sqrt, np.arctan2, np.maximum, a numpy array times or plus a symbolic vector) compute with symbolic operands instead of refusing them. Indexing raises IndexError and takes negative indices, so that a symbolic vector is a sequence; a vector divided by a scalar, 2\*\*x and abs(x) are added. The comparison with numpy in python is a test.
  - **notes:** The operators of exudyn.symbolic mean what they mean for numpy, so that one user function computes with numpy arrays and records with symbolic vectors: \* of two symbolic vectors, of two matrices or of a matrix and a vector raises a TypeError (numpy multiplies the components; use @, dot() or multiply()), as does == of two vectors; exudyn.special.deprecations.symbolicStarProduct = True restores the scalar and matrix products for the transition. New: Vector.multiply, numpy's functions with symbolic operands (np.multiply, np.dot, np.sin, np.sqrt, np.arctan2, np.maximum, a numpy array plus or times a symbolic vector), a vector divided by a scalar, 2\*\*x, abs(x), v\[-1\], sum(v); CreateSymbolicUserFunction records q and q\_t of the bodies and systems with their size.   - description: CObject::GetObjectNumber (\#2995) is set by Assemble, so an access function that calls a user function before Assemble (a reference position of ObjectUserBody) gets -1.   - description: revision2026c step RG12.3.2 (found in the pre-analysis of \#2996): ResizableConstVectorBase::SetNumberOfItems sets data = &localData\[0\] whenever the new size is not above maxNumberOfItems, also when the vector lives on the heap; the next write of more than 7 items overflows localData, and the destructor delete\[\]s localData because maxNumberOfItems \> 7. A symbolic user function sets its vector arguments on every call: ObjectGenericODE2.forceUserFunction as symbolic function crashes for 10 coordinates (0xC0000374), works for up to 7; reproduced with AddressSanitizer (stack-buffer-overflow at the second SetAll). Fix: keep data where it is in that branch.
  - **notes:** ResizableConstVector keeps its data where it is while the new size fits, and records the size of its heap memory on every allocation: symbolic vector user functions with more than 7 items no longer corrupt the heap; unit tests under AddressSanitizer, test model symbolicVectorUserFunctionTest.py (revision2026c step RG12.3.2)
  - date resolved: **2026-10-16 00:01**, date raised: 2026-10-15

- **1.13.91** `CHANGE` `LOW EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` Eigen without fused multiply-add on arm64, so that the solvers give the bits of x86-64 (#2990)
  - description: revision2026c step RG4.1.3.8: the macOS ARM run of 1.13.75 (tmp/MacOS) fails in six test models, all with LinearSolverType.EigenSparse; the dumps of the Mac agent show identical inputs, a bit-identical explicit solve and a first difference of one ulp in an implicit step. Eigen's NEON packets fuse a\*b+c (vfmaq\_f64 under \_\_ARM\_FEATURE\_FMA) whatever -ffp-contract says; without the macro they multiply and add, as SSE2 does on x86-64. Undefine it around the Eigen includes of LinearSolver.h; to be verified on macOS ARM.
  - **notes:** on arm64 Eigen multiplies and adds instead of fusing: \_\_ARM\_FEATURE\_FMA is undefined around the Eigen includes, and the DenseBase plugin Linalg/EigenPluginNoMadd.h undefines EIGEN\_HAS\_SINGLE\_INSTRUCTION\_MADD, without a change of the vendored Eigen; macOS ARM passes the whole test suite and gives the results of x86-64 (revision2026c step RG4.1.3.8)
  - date resolved: **2026-10-15 13:47**, date raised: 2026-10-12

- **1.13.48** `EXTENSION` `MEDIUM EFF` `raised by: Claude-JG` `resolved by: Claude-JG` The portable math functions of Exudyn for Python: initial conditions computed with math.sin or numpy differ per platform (#2956)
  - description: The three models left in UnresolvedOnLinux() after \#2954 compute their initial values in Python with math.sin/math.cos (createSphereQuadContact, createSphereTriangleContact: initial velocities 2\*sin(cnt\*pi/3); generalContactCylinderTest: points on a cylinder and RotationMatrixX, i.e. numpy). glibc and the MSVC UCRT round 2\*sin(4\*pi/3) differently by 1 ULP (-0x1.bb67ae8584ca9p+0 vs ...ca8p+0). With sin/cos replaced by float(exu.symbolic.sin(x)) (EM::Sin), Windows and WSL compute bit-identical ODE2 coordinates in all three models (sha256 equal); the only remaining difference is 1 ULP in np.linalg.norm of the test result (numpy 2.4.6 vs 2.2.4, SIMD summation), while sqrt(math.fsum(x\*x)) agrees. Needed: a documented, vectorized way to call EM::Sin, ... from Python (e.g. a small pybind submodule exudyn.math with sin, cos, ... taking float or numpy arrays), used by rigidBodyUtilities (RotationMatrixX, ...) and by test models; and a platform-independent norm for test results. Changes the Windows references of the affected models (generalContactCylinderTest rel. 4e-5).
  - **notes:** The test models compute their initial values with exudyn.cMath, so that generalContactCylinderTest, createSphereTriangleContact and createSphereQuadContact agree on Windows and Linux to the last bit; UnresolvedOnLinux() is empty (revision2026c steps RG4.1.3.7, RG11.10.7)
